acv.quote: We proposed six hundred K a year.

data.reason: Angela, the COO, signed with Adyen after we never showed a store return or a rollout plan. Tom thought Raj decided and that we had already won the web side.

trigger.action: Lead with online orders that stores can't see or return.
trigger.why: Returns broke last holiday season, and Angela, the COO, reportedly watched the returns queue in a store.
trigger.quote: The store couldn't see the online order

decider.action: Tell the COO one company answers for both tills and website.
decider.why: Angela signed with Adyen. Tom met her only once and treated Raj, the CTO, as the decider.
decider.quote: I don't want two vendors pointing at each other.

competitor.action: Answer store worries: installs, wifi drops, tills down on Saturdays.
competitor.why: Raj said Adyen brought a retail team. After that, 11 of 14 questions were about stores. This is secondhand.
competitor.quote: Raj forwarded me a list of 14 questions and 11 of them were about stores.

message.action: Replace the 'line has disappeared' claim with a step-by-step till return.
message.why: Bev, head of store operations, dismissed our one-platform slide and asked how a return works at the till.

proof.action: Add a retailer story showing store rollout dates and who installs.
proof.why: Angela wanted to talk to the retailer in our case study. We also had no rollout plan to show.

words.action: Say 'the tills' and 'one customer, one basket', not 'point of sale'.
words.why: Bev said it this way every time, while we kept saying 'in-person payments' and 'point of sale'.
words.quote: One system for the tills and the website.
